correctness.rationale: The projector onto the eigenvalue a of L is (bI−L−bJ/v)/(b−a), as verified by its action on all three eigenspaces. At nonedges the a- and b-projectors therefore give −C/v and (C−1)/v. At edges the numerator of the kernel entry is (1−e^(−Bt))+U(e^(−At)−e^(−Bt)), where A=a^α, B=b^α, and U=(v−k+s)/(r−s)≥0 by the adjacency spectral radius bound for the complement. The diagonals are at least 1/v by positivity of spectral-projector diagonals. For q(t)=1−C e^(−At)+(C−1)e^(−Bt), the ratio of the two derivative terms is (b/a)^(1−α) exp((B−A)t). This gives strict positivity for t>0 at α≤1 (including α=1 where q'(0)=0), and one strict minimum followed by one positive zero for α>1. Row sums are one and each row has h identical potentially negative nonedges, giving exactly 1+2h[−q(t)]_+/v. Symmetry gives the same column norm. The derivative crossing gives the displayed unique peak time. For ε=α−1, q(t)/t extends analytically at zero with expansion −Ca log(b/a) ε + Ca(b−a)t/2 + O(ε²+εt+t²); the implicit root is positive for small ε>0 and by uniqueness is the recovery root. Substituting t_pk=log(b/a)ε/(b−a)+O(ε²) into the quadratic expansion gives the claimed norm coefficient. In u=a^α t, the root is trapped on either side of log C by convergence on compact positive intervals; at the peak u→0 and (b/a)^α u→∞, giving q→1−C. At t=0 the matrix is I. No graph-uniform asymptotics are inferred.
